question: Can an exact securely Harappan stone-weight object be joined to its measured mass and authenticated ancient marks on that same object?
result: No qualifying inscribed-weight anchor found in this bounded review.

scope.primary_sources: Hemmy in Marshall1931 chapterXXIX pp589–598; Hemmy in Mackay1938 chapterXVII plus AppendixII (public20-page extract); Vats1940 volI weights pp360–364 via existing OCR, with original360–361 visually checked; volII plateCXVIII visually checked.
scope.web_search: Two targeted search batches for Harappan/Indus/Mohenjo-daro weights with inscriptions, incisions or marks; official museum/excavator leads inspected. Parent independently reviews Kenoyer2010.
scope.exclusions: Nearby inscribed seals, inferred metrological labels, Western Asian weights of disputed Indus attribution, modern catalogue numbers, and unmeasured marked artifacts do not satisfy the same-object anchor requirement.

findings.claim: Author explicitly reports no inscription or mark indicating value on examined weights.
findings.verified: Printed596 visually checked;589 text layer inspected.
findings.short_quote: No inscription nor mark of value has been found on any of the weights.
findings.limit: Statement about this historical reported collection, not proof that no inscribed weight can ever exist. Do not accept the following author inference that traders were illiterate; absence of labels does not entail that.

findings.locator: printed361; plateCXVIII, weights1–31, PDF244 in existing plates scan
findings.claim: Mass, object ID, material and provenance are available for specific weights, but no ancient inscription/value mark is authenticated by these entries and depicted views.
findings.limit: Some faces are not shown; no autopsy or detection of lost paint. Visible modern Arabic catalogue labels and natural stone bands are not ancient sign inscriptions.

findings.provenance: Susa; a proposed Indus-type attribution by Belaiew is being criticized by Hemmy.
findings.claim: Real published mass-plus-stroke descriptions, but not secure Harappan anchors. No exact museum/field IDs or mark drawings in this excerpt. Hemmy argues their marks and distributions do not justify the proposed Indus metrology.
findings.limit: Do not assign any M77 identity or transfer the proposed quarter/sixfold interpretations to Indus signs.

measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.plate: CXVIII nos4 and13 (two views of one object)
measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.mark_depiction: No authenticated ancient inscription in the described/depicted views.
measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.cautions: Edges and corners broken; reported mass not reconstructed ideal mass. OCR incorrectly has2052.8; original page shows2652.8.

measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.mark_depiction: No authenticated ancient inscription in described/depicted view.
measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.cautions: Stone mottling is not script; one published view does not inventory every face.

measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.mark_depiction: No authenticated ancient inscription in described/depicted view.
measured_but_not_inscription_anchors.cautions: OCR mistakenly gives4363; original page reads4368. No inference from pictorial size, since plate cutouts are not proportional.

secondary_or_museum_search_leads_not_use.observation: Museum exhibition page gives approximately16kg and cuneiform, but explicitly Mesopotamia; a Harappan-themed exhibition category does not make the object Harappan.
secondary_or_museum_search_leads_not_use.status: Rejected geographical/script mismatch; no separate image authentication in this task.

secondary_or_museum_search_leads_not_use.observation: NationalMuseumNewDelhi collection description reports no inscription/value mark on the displayed Indus weights.
secondary_or_museum_search_leads_not_use.status: Corroborating search lead only; core result rests on preserved primary sources.

next_discriminating_evidence: An object-specific excavation/museum ID joined to calibrated mass, material, archaeological context and images of all faces showing demonstrably ancient marks. A short repeated stroke mark alone needs exclusion of catalogue numbering, damage and manufacture. Search should target a concrete published exception to the historical uninscribed-weight statement, not retune a mass unit until an unrelated sign fits.
limits: Not exhaustive across all Indus excavations or modern collections. No semantic, phonetic, numerical-sign or commodity reading follows from these sources.
